summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -2 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; risk 0; energy 0; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Cheese +15.3%; weakest: Lean hogs -18.7%. Key releases ahead: US Average Hourly Earnings m/m (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Non-Farm Employment Change (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Unemployment Rate (11-06 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.95% (-33 bp in a month), 2-year 4.61% (-22 bp); 2s10s curve +34 bp (-11 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.03% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.48 (-0.7% in a month, +3.3% YTD). USD/BRL 5.464 (+4.6% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.663 (-0.6%); USD/MXN 18.57 (+2.3%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -0.9% in a month (+12.6% YTD); VIX 16.9. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 88.87 $/bbl (+0.8% in a month), Brent 95.67, ULSD 4.240 $/gal (-3.6%), natural gas 2.98 (-11.3%). Crude little changed on the month. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -3.3% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.1%, Hang Seng -0.5%, yuan +0.6% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 7 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (21%); S&P GSCI -4.8% in a month; gold -1.9%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
